description: Ground-truth labels for the customer-support-triage benchmark, v2. Copied from tooling/graders/ground_truth/phase2_triage.json (v1, sha256 6ca3763f32abfe3a5b8dfa56662c9083f91f81c2c3d06d3117bfb974367669d1) with the D3 alignment to the task brief (PREREGISTRATION.md section 8, grader-defects.md, tooling/graders/v2/CHANGES.md): (1) the three spam-or-noise tickets 004/009/021 are credited 'n/a' urgency, matching the brief's definition of n/a ('for noise/spam where urgency doesn't apply') — v1 labeled them 'low', a value the brief reserves for real-but-batchable work, and 64 of 64 prior-corpus cells answered n/a; (2) ticket 029 (extortion) is resolved to the brief's rules-of-the-road reading — extortion threats are spam-or-noise — with urgency n/a; v1 said security-incident/urgent, contradicting the brief the models were graded against. The v2 brief (tooling/tasks/v2/task_triage.md) removes 'extortion' from the security-incident gloss so brief and ground truth agree. Each ticket gets a primary category from a fixed vocabulary plus an urgency level. Some tickets have a 'related_to' field linking duplicates / follow-ups to their original.
